summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and the deterministic gate blocked the run. Studio did not run: simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed is false, and no artifacts were produced. The stated reason is that a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, but the extracted floorplan and power_w are empty. The scenario is Processor A from the paper, with 28 W total power, 195 mm2 die area, 4 metal layers, 11 material layers, a heat sink at 3.3e3 W/m2K and a package at 2.0e3 W/m2K. The paper's experiment is a steady-state 3D thermal grid solve with vectorless worst-case verification by LP, using CHOLMOD, Gurobi, spectral sparsification and multilevel AMG. It is not a Studio-style 2D problem. The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so even if it had run there would be no transient trace. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no Ascend910 or ATPlace pinned sizes were used, so there is no generated input.flp or one-row input.ptrace and no source commit or placement assumption to report. No Studio temperature exists, and the paper's observable is the Figure 3 per-node worst-case temperature distribution, which has no extracted numeric values or units. comparison_valid is false, so no numerical comparison is made. The two results differ in location (per-node distribution vs. none), aggregation (LP worst case over power ensembles vs. a single power vector), regime (3D steady vectorless vs. no run), and boundary conditions (equivalent heat transfer coefficients vs. an unmapped Studio package). Only a qualitative statement is supportable: the paper's worst-case temperatures depend on the power-bound constraints and the 3D stack and cooling, which a fixed-power 2D run could not reproduce. The final verdict is no replication and no validated comparison, and nothing here claims exact replication.
limitations: Studio did not run (status skipped); there is no simulated output of any kind.
Verdict is not_2d_applicable: the paper is a 3D mesh with 11 material and 4 metal layers, which a 2D model cannot reproduce.

No block-level floorplan, per-block power, die dimensions, layer thicknesses/conductivities, ambient temperature, or power-bound parameters are published; only 28 W and 195 mm2 aggregates are available.

The paper's observable is a per-node worst-case temperature over LP-derived power ensembles (Figure 3); no numeric values or units were extracted, so it cannot be compared to a single-power-vector result.
Cooling is given only as equivalent heat transfer coefficients with no package, TIM or interposer geometry, so it cannot be mapped to a Studio package without extra assumptions.
The paper's contribution is solver runtime and error on 25K to 2.0M node grids (CHOLMOD, Gurobi, spectral sparsification, multilevel AMG), not a thermal result a Studio run could replicate.
The linked CHOLMOD and Gurobi URLs are third-party solver references, not pinned input assets; no paper repository, code or config is available.
Gate input errors include evidence lacking a valid page or asset locator, missing cited observable and regime, and unresolved adversarial and independent checks; independently_verified is false.
No numerical comparison is valid and exact replication is not claimed; any future Studio run would be an illustrative construction with runner-generated geometry and power.

The paper models a full 3D mesh thermal grid with 11 material layers and 4 metal layers. A 2D Studio model cannot reproduce this vertical stack, so the 3D mismatch is decisive.

The paper's output is a worst-case temperature over an ensemble of power vectors from LP-based vectorless verification. A Studio run uses a single fixed power vector, so the observables are not equivalent.

Cooling is represented only by equivalent heat transfer coefficients (heat sink 3.3e3 and package 2.0e3 W/m2K) with no interposer, TIM or package geometry. It cannot be mapped to a Studio package model without added assumptions.

No block-level floorplan, block dimensions, or per-block powers are published, so no same-scenario geometry and power set exists. Only 28 W total and 195 mm2 total die area are given, and total power cannot be split without a published rule.

The paper's solver (CHOLMOD Cholesky with spectral sparsification and multilevel AMG), optimizer (Gurobi LP), and benchmarks (runtime and error on grids of 25K to 2M nodes) differ from a Studio thermal solver. The paper's temperature outputs are method-comparison artifacts, so a Studio run is not a replication.
The setup is steady-state with no transient, controller or reliability simulation. Thermal integrity verification is only motivated qualitatively and no reliability model is used.
No bundled Studio package/material assumptions are supplied in the packet, so none are asserted or attributed to the paper.

Since the paper publishes only aggregate power and die area, any Studio run would be a separate illustrative construction at best. Its coordinates and powers would be runner-generated, kept distinct from paper-derived facts, and not compared numerically to the paper's temperatures.
